question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The principal, along with (a)/ two senior teachers, (b)/ were planning (c)/ a visit to the flood-hit village. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a subject is followed by "along with / together with / as well as / in addition to / with", the verb agrees with the first subject and not with the noun that comes after the phrase. The subject here is "The principal" (singular), so "were planning" must be "was planning".

◦ Corrected sentence: The principal, along with two senior teachers, was planning a visit to the flood-hit village.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The principal, along with" is proper, because "along with" only adds a phrase and does not make the subject plural.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "two senior teachers," is proper, as an added phrase set off by a comma, with "two" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "a visit to the flood-hit village." is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "visit".

 

NOTE

 

• The teacher, along with the students, is; The boy, together with his parents, was; The captain, in addition to the players, has (the verb agrees with the first subject).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Neither of the two (a)/ candidates were (b)/ present at (c)/ the venue. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Neither of" + a plural noun takes a singular verb, because "neither" means "not one of the two". So "candidates were" must be "candidates was".

◦ Corrected sentence: Neither of the two candidates was present at the venue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Neither of the two" is proper, with "of" followed by a specific plural group.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "present at" is proper, with the correct preposition "at" after "present" in the sense of "being there".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the venue." is proper, with "the venue" as a specific place.

 

NOTE

 

• Neither of the boys is, Either of the roads is, Each of the girls has, One of the players was (singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Fish and chips (a)/ is a popular (b)/ dish in Britain. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. Two nouns joined by "and" that name one dish or one idea take a singular verb. "Fish and chips" is a single dish, so the singular "is" is correct.

◦ Sentence as given: Fish and chips is a popular dish in Britain.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Fish and chips" is proper, because the two nouns together name one dish.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is a popular" is proper, with the singular verb "is" agreeing with the single dish and "a" used before the consonant sound of "popular".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "dish in Britain." is proper, because the name of a single country takes no article.

 

NOTE

 

• Bread and butter is, Slow and steady wins the race (one idea, singular verb); but Ram and Shyam are (two persons, plural verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Physics are (a)/ regarded as the (b)/ foundation of all (c)/ modern sciences. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The names of subjects and branches of study that end in "-s" (physics, mathematics, economics, politics, athletics) take a singular verb. So "Physics are" must be "Physics is".

◦ Corrected sentence: Physics is regarded as the foundation of all modern sciences.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "regarded as the" is proper, because "regarded as" is the correct passive expression.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "foundation of all" is proper, with "of" correctly used after "foundation".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "modern sciences." is proper, with "all" followed by a plural noun.

 

NOTE

 

• Physics is, Economics is, Politics is, Athletics is (a subject name ending in "-s" takes a singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

A number of passengers (a)/ at the airport (b)/ was stranded (c)/ due to dense fog. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "A number of" + a plural noun means "many" and takes a plural verb. The subject here is "A number of passengers", so "was stranded" must be "were stranded".

◦ Corrected sentence: A number of passengers at the airport were stranded due to dense fog.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "A number of passengers" is proper, with "a number of" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "at the airport" is proper, with "the airport" as a specific place.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "due to dense fog." is proper, because "fog" is an uncountable noun and takes no article here.

 

NOTE

 

• A number of students are (= many, plural verb); The number of students is (= the total, singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Although the report (a)/ was prepared by many hands, (b)/ it is you (c)/ who has to defend it. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the pattern "It is I / you / he who …", the verb in the "who" clause agrees with the pronoun before "who". "You" takes a plural verb, so "who has to defend it" must be "who have to defend it".

◦ Corrected sentence: Although the report was prepared by many hands, it is you who have to defend it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Although the report" is proper, with "although" introducing a clause of contrast.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "was prepared by many hands," is proper, with the singular verb "was" agreeing with "report".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "it is you" is proper, because "it is" introduces the emphasised pronoun.

 

NOTE

 

• It is I who am, It is you who are, It is he who is (the verb agrees with the pronoun before "who").

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The wounded (a)/ in the accident (b)/ was rushed (c)/ to the nearest hospital. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The" + an adjective used for a group of people (the wounded, the poor, the injured) is plural and takes a plural verb. So "was rushed" must be "were rushed".

◦ Corrected sentence: The wounded in the accident were rushed to the nearest hospital.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The wounded" is proper, with "the" used before an adjective to name a group.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "in the accident" is proper, with "the accident" as a specific event.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "to the nearest hospital." is proper, with "the" used before the superlative "nearest".

 

NOTE

 

• The poor are, The rich are, The injured were (plural verb after "the" + adjective).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The district is largely agricultural, (a)/ and the soil is fertile, (b)/ so nearly two-thirds of (c)/ the land are under cultivation. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "fraction / per cent / half / rest + of + noun", the verb agrees with the noun after "of". "The land" is singular, so "are" must be "is".

◦ Corrected sentence: The district is largely agricultural, and the soil is fertile, so nearly two-thirds of the land is under cultivation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The district is largely agricultural," is proper, with the adverb "largely" modifying the adjective "agricultural".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "and the soil is fertile," is proper, with the singular verb "is" agreeing with "soil".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "so nearly two-thirds of" is proper, with "nearly" modifying the fraction and "so" showing result.

 

NOTE

 

• Two-thirds of the land is (singular noun); Two-thirds of the students are (plural noun); Half of the milk is.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Everyone who were (a)/ invited to the seminar (b)/ received a folder (c)/ and a pen. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Everyone, everybody, someone, anyone, nobody" are singular and take a singular verb, even in a "who" clause. So "who were" must be "who was".

◦ Corrected sentence: Everyone who was invited to the seminar received a folder and a pen.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "invited to the seminar" is proper, with the correct preposition "to" after "invited".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "received a folder" is proper, with the singular verb "received" and "a" before the consonant sound of "folder".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and a pen." is proper, with "a" used before the consonant sound of "pen".

 

NOTE

 

• Everyone is, Someone was, Nobody knows, Anybody who wants can join (singular).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Either the teacher or the students (a)/ has to (b)/ clean the classroom (c)/ before the assembly. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When two subjects are joined by "either … or", the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. The nearer subject is the plural "the students", so "has to" must be "have to".

◦ Corrected sentence: Either the teacher or the students have to clean the classroom before the assembly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Either the teacher or the students" is proper, with "either" correctly paired with "or".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "clean the classroom" is proper, with the base verb "clean" after "to" and "the classroom" as a specific place.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "before the assembly." is proper, with "the assembly" as a specific event.

 

NOTE

 

• Either the boys or the girl is; Either the girl or the boys are; Neither he nor they are (the nearer subject decides).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The loss was heavy, (a)/ and the auditors concluded (b)/ that the manager, rather than (c)/ his assistants, are to blame. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a subject is followed by "rather than / no less than / more than", the verb agrees with the first subject. The first subject is "the manager", so "are to blame" must be "is to blame".

◦ Corrected sentence: The loss was heavy, and the auditors concluded that the manager, rather than his assistants, is to blame.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The loss was heavy," is proper, with the singular verb "was" agreeing with "loss".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "and the auditors concluded" is proper, with the past tense "concluded" agreeing with the past clause before it.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "that the manager, rather than" is proper, with "that" introducing the noun clause.

 

NOTE

 

• The manager, rather than his assistants, is; The teacher, no less than the students, was (the first subject decides).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Gulliver's Travels were (a)/ written by Jonathan Swift (b)/ in the year 1726 (c)/ and remains popular. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The title of a book, film or other work is treated as one thing and takes a singular verb, even if the title looks plural. So "Gulliver's Travels were" must be "Gulliver's Travels was".

◦ Corrected sentence: Gulliver's Travels was written by Jonathan Swift in the year 1726 and remains popular.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "written by Jonathan Swift" is proper, with "by" introducing the doer in a passive sentence.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "in the year 1726" is proper, with "in" used before a year.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and remains popular." is proper, with the singular verb "remains" agreeing with the single title.

 

NOTE

 

• Gulliver's Travels is, Little Women was, The Arabian Nights is (a title takes a singular verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The police (a)/ has arrested (b)/ three suspects (c)/ in connection with the robbery. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Police" is a collective noun that is always plural, so it takes a plural verb. So "has arrested" must be "have arrested".

◦ Corrected sentence: The police have arrested three suspects in connection with the robbery.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The police" is proper, with "the" used before "police" and the noun understood as plural.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "three suspects" is proper, with "three" followed by a plural noun.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "in connection with the robbery." is proper, with the fixed phrase "in connection with".

 

NOTE

 

• always plural: police, cattle, people, poultry, gentry: The police are, The people were.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Both of the answers is (a)/ correct, but the (b)/ examiner will accept (c)/ only the first one. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Both" always means two and takes a plural verb. So "Both of the answers is" must be "Both of the answers are". (Compare "Either of" and "Neither of", which take a singular verb.)

◦ Corrected sentence: Both of the answers are correct, but the examiner will accept only the first one.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "correct, but the" is proper, with "but" joining two contrasting clauses.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "examiner will accept" is proper, with "will" followed by the base verb "accept".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "only the first one." is proper, with "the" used before the ordinal "first".

 

NOTE

 

• Both of the boys are, Both are (always plural); but Either of the boys is, Neither of the boys is (singular).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The old house was (a)/ sold last year, (b)/ but its furniture (c)/ were left behind. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Furniture" is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb. So "were left behind" must be "was left behind".

◦ Corrected sentence: The old house was sold last year, but its furniture was left behind.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The old house was" is proper, with the singular verb "was" agreeing with "house".

 

• Part (b) is correct — "sold last year," is proper, because "last year" takes no article or preposition.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "but its furniture" is proper, with the possessive "its" referring to the singular "house".

 

NOTE

 

• uncountable nouns take a singular verb: furniture is, luggage was, advice is, information was.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The cost of living (a)/ in big cities (b)/ have risen sharply. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "The cost of living …", the subject is the singular noun "cost". The noun after "of" does not decide the verb, so "have risen" must be "has risen".

◦ Corrected sentence: The cost of living in big cities has risen sharply.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The cost of living" is proper, with the singular noun "cost" as the head of the subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "in big cities" is proper, with "in" showing place and "big cities" plural.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "have risen" in part (c) does not agree with the singular subject "cost".

 

NOTE

 

• The cost of goods has, The price of vegetables has (the head noun before "of" decides the verb).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Nobody in the team (a)/ were aware of (b)/ the new rule. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Nobody" is a singular indefinite pronoun and takes a singular verb. So "were aware of" must be "was aware of".

◦ Corrected sentence: Nobody in the team was aware of the new rule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Nobody in the team" is proper, with the singular pronoun "nobody" as the subject.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the new rule." is proper, with "the new rule" as a specific rule.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "were" in part (b) does not agree with the singular subject "Nobody".

 

NOTE

 

• Nobody is, Nothing was, No one has (singular indefinite pronouns).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The teacher, as well as her students, are excited about the annual excursion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. is excited about.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "As well as" only adds a phrase, and the verb agrees with the first subject. The first subject is "The teacher" (singular), so "are excited about" must be "is excited about".

◦ Corrected sentence: The teacher, as well as her students, is excited about the annual excursion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "were excited about" — this is a plural verb, and it does not agree with the singular subject "The teacher".

 

• Option 3: "have been excited about" — this is a plural verb, and it does not agree with the singular subject "The teacher".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the plural "are" does not agree with the singular subject "The teacher".

 

NOTE

 

• as well as, along with, together with, in addition to, with: the verb agrees with the first subject — The teacher, as well as her students, is.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Not only the manager but also his assistants has been blamed for the accident.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. have been blamed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "not only … but also", the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. The nearer subject is the plural "his assistants", so "has been blamed" must be "have been blamed".

◦ Corrected sentence: Not only the manager but also his assistants have been blamed for the accident.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "was blamed" — this is a singular verb, and the nearer subject "his assistants" is plural.

 

• Option 3: "is blamed" — this is a singular verb, and the nearer subject "his assistants" is plural.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the singular "has" does not agree with the nearer subject "his assistants".

 

NOTE

 

• Not only … but also, either … or, neither … nor: the nearer subject decides — Not only the boys but also the girl was, Not only the girl but also the boys were.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Neither the workers nor I are aware of the sudden change in the schedule.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. am aware.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In "neither … nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject is "I", and the present tense of "be" that goes with "I" is "am". So "are aware" must be "am aware".

◦ Corrected sentence: Neither the workers nor I am aware of the sudden change in the schedule.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "is aware" — "is" goes with he, she or it, and it is not used with "I".

 

• Option 2: "were aware" — "were" does not go with "I" in this pattern, and it also changes the tense.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "are" does not go with "I".

 

NOTE

 

• Neither he nor I am, Neither you nor I am, Neither I nor he is (the nearer subject decides).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Either of the two routes is suitable for a heavy vehicle like this.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No improvement required.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. "Either of" + a plural noun takes a singular verb, so "is suitable" is correct.

◦ Sentence as given: Either of the two routes is suitable for a heavy vehicle like this.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "are suitable" — this is a plural verb, and "either of" needs a singular verb.

 

• Option 2: "were suitable" — this is a plural verb, and "either of" needs a singular verb.

 

• Option 3: "have been suitable" — this is a plural verb, and "either of" needs a singular verb.

 

NOTE

 

• Either of the roads is, Neither of the girls was, Each of the boys has (singular verb).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Many a young man have lost their way in such a competitive world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. has lost his way.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Many a" is followed by a singular noun, a singular verb and a singular pronoun, although the meaning is "many". So "have lost their way" must be "has lost his way".

◦ Corrected sentence: Many a young man has lost his way in such a competitive world.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "have lost his way" — the pronoun "his" is correct, but the verb "have" is plural, and "many a" needs a singular verb.

 

• Option 3: "has lost their way" — the verb "has" is correct, but the pronoun "their" is plural, and it does not agree with the singular "young man".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because both the verb "have" and the pronoun "their" are plural.

 

NOTE

 

• Many a student has, Many a mother has sacrificed her comfort (singular); Many students have (plural).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The number of candidates appearing for the exam have increased sharply this year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has increased sharply.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The number of" refers to the total count and takes a singular verb. So "have increased sharply" must be "has increased sharply".

◦ Corrected sentence: The number of candidates appearing for the exam has increased sharply this year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "are increasing sharply" — this is a plural verb, and "the number of" needs a singular verb.

 

• Option 3: "were increased sharply" — this is a plural passive verb, and "increase" is used here without an object.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the plural "have" does not agree with the singular "number".

 

NOTE

 

• The number of accidents has increased (singular); A number of accidents have occurred (plural).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

Each of the exhibits in the museum are labelled with its date and origin.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. is labelled.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Each of" + a plural noun takes a singular verb. So "are labelled" must be "is labelled", which also agrees with the singular "its".

◦ Corrected sentence: Each of the exhibits in the museum is labelled with its date and origin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "were labelled" — this is a plural verb, and "each of" needs a singular verb.

 

• Option 2: "have been labelled" — this is a plural verb, and "each of" needs a singular verb.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the plural "are" does not agree with "each".

 

NOTE

 

• Each of the students has, Each of the exhibits is (singular verb).

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

The poet and novelist were honoured with the national award last year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was honoured.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When two nouns joined by "and" refer to one person (one article before both), the verb is singular. "The poet and novelist" is one person, so "were honoured" must be "was honoured".

◦ Corrected sentence: The poet and novelist was honoured with the national award last year.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "have been honoured" — this is a plural verb, and it also does not suit the past time "last year".

 

• Option 3: "are honoured" — this is a plural present-tense verb, and the sentence refers to "last year".

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because the plural "were" does not agree with a single person.

 

NOTE

 

• The poet and novelist was (one person); The poet and the novelist were (two persons).
